title: Canary rollout scratchpad - Maria Lopez
content:
Quick scratchpad for the v1.12.3 canary rollout and model-version pinning checks.

Context:
- Release contains serving runtime changes: kernel selection tweak + KV cache warmup improvement.
- Also includes default quantization profile update for latency/cost.
- Affects chat and text-generation endpoints; embeddings unaffected.

Goals:
- Validate p50/p95 latency improvements without increased error rate.
- Ensure no regression in token-completion correctness for core prompt sets.
- Confirm rollout/rollback automation works end-to-end (routing + config).

Canary plan (high level):
1) Start: 1% traffic to new variant (v1.12.3) for 30m.
2) If green -> 5% for 30m.
3) If green -> 20% for 1h.
4) If green -> 50% for 2h.
5) Final -> 100% after manual sign-off / automated checks.

Quick checklist before starting canary:
- [ ] Verify deployment artifacts: image tag gh-4321 + manifest checksum matches PR.
- [ ] Confirm model pinning config: chat-default -> model-x-v2 pinned (no auto-upgrade).
- [ ] Update route weights in staging and confirm traffic splitting via Console.
- [ ] Pre-warm KV caches on canary pool (scripts/run_kv_warmup.sh).
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler min replicas set (avoid underprovisioning during ramp).
- [ ] Notify oncall + CS (Slack #releases + #cs-oncall).

Monitoring / Success criteria (automated):
- Latency: p50 <= baseline_p50 * 1.05, p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.10.
- Errors: request_error_rate <= baseline_error_rate + 0.1% absolute and < 1% relative increase.
- Model quality: SMT eval set pass rate >= baseline - 0.5%. (run quick-eval job after each stage)
- Cost: avg cost/token not increased by > 10% without latency wins.

Rollback criteria (immediate rollback if any condition met):
- Spike in 5xxs > 0.5% absolute above baseline in 5m window.
- p95 latency breach > 30% over baseline for 15m.
- Quality regression: eval fail rate increase > 1.0% absolute.
- Customer-facing alerts (CS reports degraded behavior).

Operational runbook notes (to self):
- Use console route controls: Route = chat.default, Variant = v1.12.3-canary.
- Command to change weight via CLI: rwoodctl routes update --route chat.default --variant v1.12.3-canary --weight 5
- To rollback to previous: rwoodctl rollout rollback --route chat.default --to-previous
- If autoscaler behaves weirdly, scale down/up pool manually: rwoodctl pools set --name canary-pool --replicas 6
- If KV warmup missed: run scripts/warmup_kv_for_pool.py --pool canary-pool

Quality checks (manual/automated):
- Run small batch of canonical prompts through canary endpoint (scripts/canary_smoke.sh) - compare tokens, stop words, hallucination signals.
- Run evaluation harness: eval/harness/run_eval.sh --suite core-smoke --variant v1.12.3-canary -> produce pass/fail summary.
- Check embeddings (even though not changed) for sanity on a couple examples.

Pinned config notes:
- chat-default pinned to model-x-v2 to avoid accidental model upgrades during rollout.
- Document where pin lives: config/routes/chat-default/pinning.yaml (double-check in repo).
- If we need to unpin after release, follow post-release checklist.

Communication plan:
- Pre-rollout: post to #releases with time window + link to this doc + expected impact.
- At each milestone success: quick Slack update and update the Confluence runbook with timestamps.
- On rollback: immediate page to oncall, update ticket JIRA-RELEASE-890 with rollback reason and logs.

Things to watch for (notes):
- Saw a flake in kernel-selection A/B last week for long-context prompts - pay special attention to >2048 token sessions.
- Memory pressure on older GPU types might surface with quantization tweaks; target canary pool uses T4s only.
- Batching change might slightly reduce p50 but increase p95 for tiny requests; include distribution checks by request size.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add smoke test to CI that hits canary variant directly.
- [ ] Confirm GH-PR-4321 artifact published to staging registry.
- [ ] Run full eval suite on staging with v1.12.3 (overnight).
- [ ] Prep post-mortem template in Confluence in case of rollback.

Contacts / primary context holders:
- Oncall SRE: Jordan Lee (pager: Jordan)
- Release owner: Maria Lopez (me)
- Product owner: Priya Kapoor
- Eng lead (serving-runtime): Samir Patel

Notes to self / questions:
- If the canary shows cost regressions but latency improves, discuss tradeoff with product (Priya) before promoting.
- Double-check whether Dedicated customers have separate routing policies - we should not change those.
- Remember to re-run KV warmup script after each canary pool restart.

Scratchpad end - will convert to formal runbook if this goes green.
